newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Biota gets rights to anti-cancer compounds.
newsitem.headline: Biota gets rights to anti-cancer compounds.

text.p: Drug developer Biota Holdings Ltd on Monday it has signed an agreement with La Trobe University, Melbourne, for the exclusive worldwide rights to newly synthesised anti-cancer chemical compounds.

"The new compounds have shown encouraging results in reducing the growth of colon cancer cells in tests conducted in animals. It is anticipated that they may also be useful in treating other solid tumours such as cancers of the lung and stomach," Biota said in a statement.
The compounds had been tested in the Cancer Society Research Laboratory, University of Auckland, New Zealand.

"This is a very exciting development in the field of anti-cancer research and it holds the prospect of a substantial advance in the effectiveness of our fight against cancer", Biota chief executive officer Hugh Niall said in the statement.

"The compounds join a small number of agents that can simultaneously inhibit two enzymes involved in DNA replication. Other chemical compounds have been able to inhibit one or the other of the two enzymes and this has been shown to have an anti-cancer effect in humans and animals.
Under the Agreement with the university, additional research would be undertaken by the University before a lead compound is selected for further development and Phase I trials in humans.
Niall said this agreement was consistent with the company's strategy of continuous development of its pipeline of pharmaceutical research. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
